title: Cascade Model Radar — Dossier Section Contract (v2)
description: The canonical shape a synthesis agent must return when composing a model dossier or benchmark dossier from harvested evidence. Every claim-bearing entry carries a stance (whose kind of voice made the claim), source attribution, and a confidence rating ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' — this file standardizes on the three-level categorical scale, NOT 0..1 numeric). SLUG RULES — model_slug is the lowercase-hyphenated canonical RELEASE slug (e.g. 'claude-fable-5', 'gpt-5', 'gemini-2.5-pro'); family_slug groups releases of the same line (e.g. 'claude', 'gpt', 'gemini'); benchmark slugs are likewise lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. 'swe-bench', 'mmlu', 'arc-agi'). Dots are allowed inside slugs for version tokens (as in 'gemini-2.5-pro'). FAMILY ROLLUP — a family is a QUERY-TIME grouping over model dossiers sharing a family_slug; there is NO stored family object and this schema deliberately defines none. V2 adds OPTIONAL additive sections — model_dossier.meta_rating (capability vector + researcher-voice narrative) and benchmark_dossier.score_context (standings + dynamics) — while the numeric snapshot + axis-taxonomy contracts live in score-schema.json; v1 dossiers remain valid.

stance.description: Whose kind of voice a claim comes from. 'lab_claim' = the releasing lab's own announcement/model card/marketing. 'independent_eval' = third-party benchmark runs, structured evals, red-team reports. 'practitioner_take' = hands-on builder/creator experience reports and opinions. Per-source stance hints in sources.json are DEFAULTS; extraction may override per evidence item (e.g. a practitioner video quoting a lab benchmark table yields a lab_claim item).

confidence.description: Categorical confidence in a claim — the ONE confidence scale for this contract (three-level categorical; 0..1 numeric was considered and rejected for cross-agent consistency). 'high' = corroborated across stances or from a rigorous independent eval; 'medium' = single credible source or partially corroborated; 'low' = anecdotal, contested, or lab-only with no independent check.

slug.description: Lowercase-hyphenated canonical slug: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, with dots permitted inside version tokens. Examples — models: 'claude-fable-5', 'gpt-5', 'gemini-2.5-pro'; families: 'claude', 'gpt', 'gemini'; benchmarks: 'swe-bench', 'mmlu', 'arc-agi'.

source_ref.description: Attribution for one piece of evidence backing a claim. url should be the normalized canonical URL (dedup-comparable, matching the /cse:ingest convention: lowercased host, utm_*/fbclid/gclid + fragment + trailing slash stripped).

url.description: Normalized canonical URL of the source.

author.description: Person or outlet behind the source (e.g. 'AI Explained', 'Anthropic').

source_id.description: Optional id of the registry entry in sources.json this evidence was harvested from.

stance.description: Stance of THIS evidence item — may override the source's default stance_hint.

published_date.description: ISO date the source was published, if discoverable.

claim.description: One claim-bearing entry. Every claim carries its stance, its confidence ('low'|'medium'|'high'), and source attribution.

statement.description: Full standalone sentence carrying the specific detail/number/example from the evidence (not generic).

divergence_side.description: One side of a contested question: the position taken, which stances are on this side, and the sources arguing it.

position.description: The position this side takes, stated as a standalone sentence.

stances.description: Which stance(s) are on this side of the divergence (e.g. lab_claim on one side, practitioner_take on the other).

confidence.description: Confidence that this side's position is accurately represented by the cited sources.

divergence_entry.description: One contested question where credible sources disagree — the signal a single-stance summary would flatten. Each entry names the topic and lays out the opposing sides with position, stances, and attribution.

topic.description: What the disagreement is about (e.g. 'real-world coding ability vs. SWE-bench score').

assessment.description: Optional synthesis judgment: which side the evidence favors and why, or 'unresolved'.

axis_score.description: One scored capability axis. 'axis' is one of the 6 core axis ids — 'coding', 'reasoning', 'agentic_tool_use', 'writing_communication', 'speed', 'cost_efficiency' — or an emergent slug. RUBRIC — 'value' is an integer 0-100 scored RELATIVE to the current frontier: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong, 40-69 mid, <40 weak/unproven. The rationale is load-bearing: it MUST cite a specific score snapshot or evidence package, never vibes.

axis.description: Axis id: one of the 6 core ids ('coding', 'reasoning', 'agentic_tool_use', 'writing_communication', 'speed', 'cost_efficiency') or an emergent slug.

value.description: 0-100 score relative to the current frontier: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong, 40-69 mid, <40 weak/unproven.

rationale.description: Why this value — MUST cite a specific score snapshot or evidence package backing the number.

sources.description: Optional attribution for the evidence behind this axis score.

emergent_axis_score.description: An axis_score for an EMERGENT axis — a capability dimension the 6 core axes don't cover. Add one only when 2+ independent evidence items support the dimension; never duplicate a core axis. Same shape and rubric as axis_score, plus a REQUIRED 'definition' explaining what the axis measures and why the evidence supports adding it.

axis.description: Emergent axis slug (lowercase-hyphenated or snake_case id, distinct from all 6 core axis ids).

value.description: 0-100 score relative to the current frontier: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong, 40-69 mid, <40 weak/unproven.

rationale.description: Why this value — MUST cite a specific score snapshot or evidence package backing the number.

definition.description: REQUIRED for emergent axes: what this axis measures and why the evidence (2+ independent items) supports adding it beyond the 6 core axes.

sources.description: Optional attribution for the evidence behind this axis score.

capability_vector.description: The structured capability profile of one model release: ALL 6 core axes scored (coding, reasoning, agentic_tool_use, writing_communication, speed, cost_efficiency), plus any emergent axes the evidence supports. This shape is the canonical contract shared with score-schema.json and the TypeScript types — field names are load-bearing.

core.description: All 6 core axes scored — one axis_score per core axis id. minItems 6: a capability vector with a missing core axis is invalid; use 'insufficient_evidence' plus a low-confidence score rather than omitting an axis.

emergent.description: Optional emergent axes — only when 2+ independent evidence items support a dimension the core 6 don't cover.

synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the synthesis run that produced this vector.

model_slug.description: Optional canonical release slug this vector describes (redundant with the enclosing dossier when embedded; useful when the vector travels alone, e.g. in package type_data).

insufficient_evidence.description: Honest statement when the evidence base is thin — which axes are under-evidenced and why the scores there should be read cautiously.

divergence_flag.description: Explicit honesty marker for one place where the NUMBERS and the DISCOURSE disagree — e.g. leaderboard scores say frontier-leading coding while practitioners report real-world regressions. Distinct from divergence_entry (source-vs-source disagreement): this flags structured-score-vs-narrative divergence.

topic.description: What the divergence is about (e.g. 'agentic coding ability').

discourse_says.description: What lab claims and/or practitioner discourse say.

axis.description: Optional axis id the divergence bears on (core id or emergent slug).

assessment.description: Researcher judgment on which side the evidence favors and why, or 'unresolved'.

sources.description: Optional attribution for the discourse side of the divergence.

meta_rating.description: Researcher-voice META-RATING of one model release, synthesized from the full stored score-snapshot series plus all discourse evidence. The narrative reads like an indiscriminate researcher writing a research paper across the industry's benchmarks — deducing what the numbers mean rather than repeating them — citing specific snapshots and discourse, and staying honest about insufficiency and about places where numbers and discourse disagree.

narrative.description: Researcher-voice meta-analysis: what the benchmark record and discourse, taken together, say this model actually is. Cites specific score snapshots + discourse evidence; honest about insufficient evidence.

divergence_notes.description: Explicit honesty: every place the structured numbers and the discourse disagree.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp this meta-rating was last updated.

standing_entry.description: One model's current standing on a benchmark — a single (model, value, as-of) point derived from the stored score-snapshot series.

model_slug.description: Canonical release slug of the model holding this standing.

value.description: The score value as reported for this benchmark (in the benchmark's native metric/unit).

as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the score was reported/snapshot — the standing's freshness stamp.

metric.description: Optional metric name when the benchmark reports several (e.g. 'pass@1', 'resolved').

source_slug.description: Optional slug/id of the source or leaderboard the snapshot came from.

score_context.description: Current standings + score dynamics for one benchmark, derived from the append-only score_snapshots series stored in package type_data — grounded in stored snapshots, not vibes.

standings.description: Current top models on this benchmark with as-of dates, derived from the stored snapshot series.

dynamics.description: Score dynamics over the stored series: movement, saturation, new entrants — grounded in stored snapshots, not vibes.

as_of.description: Optional ISO timestamp this context was derived.

model_dossier.title: Model Dossier
model_dossier.description: Dossier for ONE canonical model release (one model_slug). Family-level views ('how is the claude line trending?') are computed at query time by grouping dossiers on family_slug — no family object is ever stored.

model_slug.description: Canonical RELEASE slug, lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. 'claude-fable-5', 'gpt-5', 'gemini-2.5-pro'). One dossier per release slug — this is the dossier's identity key.

family_slug.description: Groups releases of the same model line (e.g. 'claude', 'gpt', 'gemini'). Family rollup is a QUERY-TIME grouping by this field; no family object is stored.

release_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the model was publicly released/announced.

last_synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent synthesis run that produced/updated this dossier.

superseded_by.description: Optional. model_slug of the release that supersedes this one within the same family (e.g. a dossier for 'gpt-4o' pointing at 'gpt-5'). Absent while the release is current.

strengths.description: What the model is demonstrably good at. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

risks.description: Weaknesses, regressions, failure modes, safety/cost/latency concerns. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

post_release_findings.description: What emerged AFTER release day — independent evals landing, practitioner experience accumulating, quiet capability discoveries, degradation reports. This is where the dossier diverges from the launch-day narrative. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

divergence.description: Contested questions where sources DISAGREE — each entry carries the opposing positions, which stances sit on each side, and attribution. Preserving disagreement (rather than averaging it away) is the point of this section.

fit_for_our_stack.description: How this model fits OUR stack — notes grounded in org context (for Cascade HQ: Claude Code / Agent SDK harnesses, Max Plan vs API billing constraints, MCP tooling, Supabase/Next.js codebase, Steve's interactive-terminal workflow). This section is org-specific by design and is synthesized against .cascade/context/ and org memory, not just public evidence.

summary.description: 2-4 sentence bottom line: adopt / trial / watch / skip for our stack, and why.

considerations.description: Specific fit notes (integration surface, pricing/plan fit, migration cost, workflow impact). Each is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources — org-context-grounded entries may cite internal docs/memory as sources.

meta_rating.description: OPTIONAL (v2). Researcher-voice META-RATING synthesized from the full score-snapshot series plus all discourse evidence. Persisted BOTH here (artifact body) and structured on the package row as type_data.capability_vector.

benchmark_dossier.title: Benchmark Dossier
benchmark_dossier.description: Dossier for ONE benchmark (one benchmark_slug, lowercase-hyphenated, e.g. 'swe-bench', 'mmlu', 'arc-agi'). Captures what it tests, whether to trust it, how gameable it is, and who leans on it.

benchmark_slug.description: Canonical benchmark slug, lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. 'swe-bench', 'mmlu', 'arc-agi'). This is the dossier's identity key.

last_synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent synthesis run that produced/updated this dossier.

measures.description: What the benchmark actually tests — task format, domain, scoring method — stated plainly enough to judge whether a score transfers to real work.

credibility_critique.description: Known critiques of the benchmark's validity: contamination, saturation, harness sensitivity, construct-validity gaps. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

gameability.description: How the benchmark can be (or has been) gamed: training on test data, prompt/harness tuning, cherry-picked subsets, leaderboard overfitting. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

cited_by.description: Who cites this benchmark and in what capacity, with source attribution — the trail of labs, evaluators, and practitioners leaning on it.

who.description: Named actor citing the benchmark (e.g. 'Anthropic', 'AI Explained', 'Epoch AI').

stance.description: The citing actor's stance (a lab citing it in a launch post = lab_claim).

context.description: How/why they cite it (e.g. 'headline metric in the Fable 5 announcement').

popularity.description: How widely the benchmark is cited across the harvested corpus right now. 'high' = a headline metric labs lead with; 'medium' = regularly referenced; 'low' = niche/emerging or fading. Justify the rating via cited_by and credibility_critique entries rather than extra fields here.

score_context.description: OPTIONAL (v2). Standings + dynamics derived from the append-only score_snapshots series stored in the benchmark package's type_data.
